answers.1: Yellow + Green (both people-oriented, so they click socially)
answers.2: Red + Blue (Red drives decisions, Blue provides analysis and quality — complementary task focus)
answers.4: Blue (precision, method, following procedure — though a strong Red element helps under pressure)
answers.8: Green (Blue is also punctual, but reliability is Green's hallmark)
answers.10: Red (result-driven risk-taker; Yellow loves novelty too, but for getting the job done it's Red)
answers.11: Green (takes criticism personally and holds onto it quietly)
answers.12: Yellow (disorganized but a natural networker who knows who to ask)
answers.16: Red (quick, blunt snap judgments; Yellow also forms fast impressions, but Red is quickest to judge)
answers.17: All four — a balanced team needs Red's drive, Yellow's enthusiasm/communication, Green's cohesion, and Blue's quality control; no single pair is 'best'
answers.19: Yellow (Red is quick to act, but Yellow is quickest to embrace and spread new ideas)
answers.20: Red (delegates, but impatience and control drive it to take over)
answers.23: Not applicable — I'm an AI and don't have a social circle; statistically, Greens are often said to be the most common profile in the general population, but I can't observe one myself
